subject: Scope and span realignment proposal (draft)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: g.morales@orgdesign.co, peopleops@acme-talent.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Scope and span realignment proposal (draft)

Team —

I've attached a draft proposal that shifts reporting lines for parts of the Serving Runtime and Platform Observability pods to improve cross-functional ownership of latency SLAs and rollout operations. The two key moves are:

- Move Rollouts & Canaries (currently in Platform Observability) to Serving Runtime to centralize release ownership for model rollout logic.
- Create a small "Platform Ops" manager role responsible for infra-oncall coordination, bundling existing infra triage responsibilities.

Why now: our recent SLA misses and the duplication of rollout configs across two teams make it easier for regressions to slip through. The goal is to reduce handoffs and put ownership of rollout logic and canary policy in the team that ships model-serving changes.

Please review the attached org-chart-v2.pdf and role-matrix.xlsx. The linked doc has a proposed communication timeline and suggested 1:1 calibration meetings with impacted ICs. I want to be transparent with the ask: some reporting lines change, and two manager roles would be repurposed (no layoffs planned).

Open questions I want feedback on this week:
- Are the proposed spans reasonable for the two affected manager roles?
- Any concerns about perceived career-path regressions for the INF and TOOLS ICs?
- HR constraints (bumping, promotions, compensation rebanding) — Laura, can you highlight any red flags?

Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Z_scope_realign_draft
Attachments: org-chart-v2.pdf (diagram), role-matrix.xlsx (matrix with proposed scope & banding)

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com, peopleops@acme-talent.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scope and span realignment proposal (draft)

Connor —

Thanks for the clear doc. I reviewed the role-matrix and flagged three items in the Drive comments where we should either: (a) confirm that a role is being repurposed rather than eliminated, or (b) clarify the rebanding timeline. Quick notes:

- If a role is repurposed, we need to publish an internal FAQ and hold 1:1 touchpoints before the wider comms.
- Compensation: two ICs fall near the mid-point for their band; if they move under a manager with broader span we should assess a short-term comp adjustment or a clear promotion ladder.
- Bumping: avoid forced reclassification that would result in role title changes without signed consent — this is sensitive and slows optics if done poorly.

I'll draft a short HR readiness checklist by EOD and share with PeopleOps. Also recommend we run the plan by Gina (OrgDesign) for a language-first comms review — she is CC'd.

Laura Bennett
VP, People & Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

Connor / Laura —

High-level: I support centralizing rollout ownership in Serving Runtime. Operationally, it should remove a class of late-hour handoffs. My asks before we go public:

1) Put a two-week overlap window for the release engineers being transitioned so knowledge transfer is auditable (pairing sessions, runbook sign-offs).
2) Identify a single fallback operator who retains the platform-level canary kill switch for 30 days post-migration.
3) We should not increase any individual manager's direct report count above 9 without a headcount request. If we exceed that we either need an IC lead or an additional manager headcount.

If HR can map the potential rebanding costs, I can model the impact on FY26 hiring/bench and propose a headcount trade.

Marcus Lin
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

I like the direction. A couple of clarifying questions from an IC career lens:

- For the INF engineers that will move under Serving Runtime, will their promotion clock pause or continue? Some are mid-cycle and a pause would materially affect retention.
- For the proposed Platform Ops manager role, does the matrix show a Level 5 vs Level 6 expectation? That impacts comp.

If we can surface the recommended timeline for calibration and whether there are any guaranteed promotion reviews for impacted ICs in the next 6 months, that will make communications much smoother.

Thanks all for the quick input — good points. Actions I will take today:

- Add a two-week overlap window and a transfer checklist to the Drive doc (pairing sessions, runbook sign-offs, checklist owner).
- Ask Laura to circulate the HR readiness checklist and compensation impact memo; Laura, ping me when it's ready and I will review.
- I'll lower the proposed max direct reports to 9 and include an explicit headcount request template if any manager would exceed that.
- Updated doc + redlined org-chart link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3OrgChartV2 (org-chart-v2.pdf)

Tentative comms plan:
Week 0 (prep): 1:1s with impacted ICs and managers; HR FAQ drafted.
Week 1 (announce): Team-wide email with role changes + manager 1:1 schedules.
Week 3 (transition): Overlap pairing and final sign-offs.

If there are no blockers by EOD Monday, I'll schedule the 1:1s and loop in PeopleOps for offers/changes.

Connor
